To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

B cell development is determined by B cell antigen receptor specificity and surface density, and that B-1 cell development is favored by B cell antigen receptors of high affinity for self-antigen and low density of B cell antigen receptors on the cell surface.

B-1 cells are generated from B cell precursors that express a particular VH region, and that the B cell antigen receptor (BCR) specificity and BCR surface density are important in determining B-1 versus conventional B cell development.
the B-1 and B-2 cell subsets of mice are generated by different developmental pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which B cells develop into mature B cell subsets, with a particular interest in the development of B-1 cells.
the molecular and cellular basis of B cell development, and the mechanisms by which B cell antigen receptors influence B cell fate.
the development and function of B lymphocytes, and the regulation of antibody production in the mouse.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
B-1 cells are selected by BCR specificity and B-2 cells by surface density.
the B-1 cell repertoire is determined by the VH12 H chain gene, whereas the B-2 cell repertoire is determined in part by the VH12 and in part by the VHB1- 8 H chain gene.

the B-1 cell fate is favored by BCRs that are highly cross-reactive with self antigens, and are expressed in low density on the cell surface, whereas the B-2 fate is favored by highly cross-reactive BCRs expressed in high density on the cell surfaces.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
B-1 and B-2 cells have distinct BCR requirements for their development, and that BCR density and antigenic stimulation are important in determining B cell lineage commitment.
B-1 cell development is favored by BCRs of low affinity and low surface density.
B-1 cells arise from a distinct precursor, but are selected in the periphery by a unique combination of antigenic stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
B-1 cells are selected by the same signals that drive B-1 cell development in the absence of the VH12 transgene.
BCR specificity and density together determine B cell development.
B-2 and B-1 cell development is determined by the relative strength of the BCRs, and the relative strength of BCR signaling.
